newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: LWR SEES GAINS FROM LOWER NZ DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: LWR SEES GAINS FROM LOWER NZ DOLLAR.

text.p: Textile manufacturer LWR Industries said on Wednesday it expects to profit from the recent fall in the New Zealand dollar.
Sales to customers outside New Zealand comprised 39 percent of turnover in 1996/97, although most manufacturing for offshore customers was also conducted offshore.
"It certainly would help our situation in Australia, there is no doubt about it, and for repatriating profits from Australia," Corporate Services Manager Glenn Keen told Reuters.
Keen said sales in 1997/98 had begun encouragingly but he was reluctant to forecast that continuing through the year.
"It's a very pleasing start for us. It's not coming from any one sector. It's occurring with all our products."
Earlier, the company reported a flat June year pre-tax profit of $13.2 million in a tough trading environment.
LWR said two years ago it could not survive with the New Zealand dollar above 85 Australian cents.
"It has come back to more realistic levels but it is only at that stage. It needs to go further before we can realistically say 'this is really terrific'," Keen said.
The New Zealand dollar is now trading at around 86.3 Australian cents from over 92 cents in June and 95 cents two years ago.
During the year LWR's gross margins improved despite the conditions.
The higher margins came from more branded product being sold and better margins commanded from specialised and quality imported products such as thermal underwear.
LWR would continue to import a greater proportion of its sales, Keen said.
It expects further rationalisation with one or two of its units not yet "properly positioned".
"It is our strategy of prune and grow. If things aren't performing the way we want we will spin them off and hopefully bring on something else that will grow stronger," Keen said.
